key_insight: An adsorbate-free graph neural network screens dissociative water adsorption on nickel using only bare-metal geometry and proposed binding-site anchors.
engineering_relevance: The framework reduces reliance on exhaustive DFT screening and enables searches for favorable OH*+H* configurations on nickel nanoparticles containing up to approximately 3,000 atoms.
method: Define candidate O- and H-binding sites as sets of Ni anchor atoms.
Build local graphs from anchors and surrounding Ni atoms in MACE-relaxed bare structures.
Use separate GNNs to predict adsorption energy and whether proposed binding sites survive DFT relaxation.
evidence_signal: The energy model achieved 0.031 eV internal-validation MAE; tests on unseen Ni55, Ni91, Ni130 clusters and larger surface cells supported transferability, especially for relative-energy ranking.
watch_item: Quantitative accuracy varies across systems, so use the retention classifier conservatively and verify priority candidates with DFT.
paper_title: Adsorbate-Free Screening of Dissociative Water Adsorption on Nickel Nanoparticles via Graph Neural Networks
